subject: Private deployment: cryptographic separation, operator visibility & access matrix
messages:
From: Mark Turner <mturner@medflowhealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Contracts Team <contracts@medflowhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 30 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions about privacy controls for private VPC deployment

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're preparing our internal security checklist ahead of a procurement review and have a few clarifying questions about Redwood's Private deployment (VPC/on-prem) model that are blocking us from approving the DPA redlines: 

1) Customer-managed keys: can you confirm whether Redwood operators can ever decrypt customer plaintext when a customer-managed KEK/HSM is used? If there are break-glass procedures, what explicit controls and approvals are required?
2) Operator access: what operator roles exist and what actions can they perform against runtime state (KV cache, model weights, logs)? We need a simple access matrix.
3) Subprocessors: please provide a current list of subprocessors, their roles (storage, telemetry, support), and where they are located geographically.
4) Cross-border transfers: if we deploy in eu-west-1, will any telemetry/logging or backups be routed outside the EU by default?
5) Audit artifacts: what logs/audit data are available to us (SIEM integration, retention) and do they include any plaintext examples?

I'm copying our contracts team (Anya will join later) and our legal counsel. If you can send an interim answer and any artifacts (DPA redline, network diagram, subprocessors list) that would be great — we can then schedule a 30-min ops session.

Best,
Mark
VP, IT Security
MedFlow Health

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Mark Turner <mturner@medflowhealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 May 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions about privacy controls for private VPC deployment

Hi Mark — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front and a proposed next step below; attached are a DPA with our suggested clarifications, a high-level network diagram, and the current subprocessors CSV. More detail follows.

Short answers:
- Customer-managed keys (KMIP/HSM): With customer-managed KEK where the KEK is held in the customer's KMS/HSM and only a wrapped data key is present on Redwood nodes, Redwood operators do not have the ability to derive plaintext. We run with envelope encryption; operator actions cannot unwrap without explicit customer escrow or HSM-coordinated operations.
- Operator access: We segment operator roles: "infra-ops" (node health, restarts), "platform-ops" (deployments, config), "support-readonly" (troubleshooting metadata). None of these roles can decrypt customer data when customer keys are enforced. I attach a proposed access matrix.
- Subprocessors & geos: attached list includes storage providers (us-west/eu), observability vendors (us-east), and a third-party support provider (apac). We can provide a geofenced list for eu-only deployments.
- Cross-border: By default telemetry is region-local, but backups and some observability pipelines may cross regions depending on the deployment model. For eu-west-1 with customer-managed keys and geofence option enabled, we can guarantee no backups leave the EU without an explicit contractual exception.
- Audit artifacts: Audit logs (configuration, operator actions, key-wrap events) are available via a secure log export to your SIEM. We do not include customer plaintext in logs; any sampled payloads are redacted unless agreed otherwise in a runbook and with your explicit approval.

Next step: Kimberly (legal) and Rishi (security) are copied. Can we schedule a 30–45 minute ops + legal workshop this week to walk through the DPA redlines and the break-glass workflow? I propose Thu 31 May 09:00 PT or Fri 1 Jun 10:00 PT.

Regards,
Soojin Lee
Enterprise Account Executive — Redwood Inference

Attachments: DPA_redlines_v2.pdf (summary of changes), redwood-network-diagram.png (high-level), subprocessors_20280530.csv

From: Mark Turner <mturner@medflowhealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Contracts Team <contracts@medflowhealth.com>, Anya Petrov <anya.petrov@regulus-legal.com>
Date: Wed, 31 May 2028 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions about privacy controls for private VPC deployment

Soojin — thanks for the quick reply and the attachments. A couple of follow-ups from our side before the workshop: 

- Break-glass specifics: we need the exact approval chain and technical steps for an emergent unwrapping request (who approves, what logging/notification happens, are keys escrowed or does Redwood perform a joint HSM operation). Can you provide a short runbook excerpt?
- KV cache: is the inference KV cache encrypted at rest with the same envelope approach? Are caches flushed on node recycle and what telemetry remains after a restart?
- Subprocessor contract: can you confirm whether subprocessors are bound by the same DPA terms (data access, deletion, and audit)? We'd like to see contractual language or a standard addendum.
- EU geofence: please confirm the mechanism you use to enforce region-only backups (is it configuration, policy, or a contractual commitment?).

Anya from Regulus is copied for review on the DPA redlines. If you can drop the runbook excerpt and the subprocessors contract pointer into the shared Drive link prior to the workshop that would save time.

Best,
Mark

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Mark Turner <mturner@medflowhealth.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 01 Jun 2028 10:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions about privacy controls for private VPC deployment

Hi Mark / Anya — copying the security team and legal counsel into a consolidated reply. Below are the concrete details you requested; I have also attached a short "Emergency Unwrap Runbook" excerpt and the subprocessors contract template.

1) Break-glass and key control (technical & approvals):
- We support two models for emergency access: (A) Customer-key-only: customer must perform HSM-assisted unwrapping (Redwood cannot unwrap). (B) Joint-escrow: a dual-control HSM key share model where both parties (customer security owner + Redwood security on-call) must sign the unwrapping operation; all requests require:
  * documented business justification,
  * written authorization from an approved contact list,
  * multi-party HSM operation (FIPS 140-2 compliant) recorded in the audit log.
- All unwrap operations are logged, immutable, and forwarded to a customer-designated SIEM endpoint. We will not perform unilateral unwrapping except with the joint-escrow workflow and recorded approvals.

2) KV cache and runtime state:
- KV cache is encrypted at rest per-node with envelope encryption using a data key wrapped by the customer KEK (when configured). On node recycle, the cache is zeroed; restart will rebuild cache from encrypted persisted segments if configured — ephemeral data is not retained beyond retention window (configurable).
- Telemetry retained post-restart is metadata-only (request IDs, latency, error codes). We do not persist model inputs or unredacted outputs in telemetry by default.

3) Subprocessors & contractual binding:
- Subprocessors are contractually bound to the DPA terms and the data processing addendum. The attached CSV lists each subprocessor, role, and country. For eu-only deployments we offer an addendum that enforces EU-only processing for telemetry and backups.

4) Cross-border controls / geofence mechanism:
- Geofence is enforced by deployment configuration + routing policy in the control plane; we additionally offer a contractual guarantee in the addendum that specifies region-bound backups. For customers requiring absolute data sovereignty we offer an on-prem package that keeps all persisted artifacts inside customer-controlled storage.

5) Audit & retention:
- Audit trails for operator actions, key-wrap events, and break-glass approvals are available for export via secure delivery (S3 presigned, HTTPS push to your SIEM). Retention is configurable; default is 90 days with enterprise tiers supporting extended retention.

Attachments included: "Emergency_Unwrap_Runbook_excerpt.txt" (runbook steps), "subprocessors_20280530.csv" (contract names + geos), "DPA_redlines_v2.pdf" (legal redlines).

If that level of detail looks good we can sign the DPA addendum for EU geofence and finalise the joint-escrow language. I'll be on the Thu 31 May 09:00 PT slot if you confirm — otherwise Fri 1 Jun 10:00 PT also works.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Director, Product Security — Redwood Inference

From: Mark Turner <mturner@medflowhealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Anya Petrov <anya.petrov@regulus-legal.com>, Contracts Team <contracts@medflowhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Jun 2028 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions about privacy controls for private VPC deployment

Kimberly / Soojin — this is exactly the level of detail we needed, thank you. A few short notes: 

- The joint-escrow HSM flow and immutable logging meet our requirements in principle.
- Please include the explicit clause that subprocessors will be bound to the DPA (we saw the language in the CSV but want it in the addendum itself).
- For EU production we want the geofence addendum to state "no backups, logs, or telemetry shall be transferred outside the EU except by prior written exception". That can be a bespoke provision in the DPA addendum.

Let's lock the Thu 31 May 09:00 PT workshop (please send calendar invite). After the workshop we expect to move to final signatures (DocuSign link) and a one-week ops runbook review with our infrastructure team.

Thanks again — looking forward to the call.

Best regards,
Mark
VP, IT Security
MedFlow Health
